title: Worldseed indie-game UI: readable fonts, centered dialog, full-screen background
summary: Make the Worldseed UI look and read like a real indie game: readable pixel fonts, story text in a centered dialog, and a full-screen background.
description: Context: the captured screen at http://localhost:5173/ shows the intro as unstyled black text on a white page (IntroScreen uses class intro-screen, which has no CSS). During play, GameLayout puts the story text in a narrow right-hand sidebar (3fr/1fr grid) instead of over the scene. Desired behavior: readable fonts, story text in a centered dialog, and a full-screen background on both the intro and the game. Expected result: a player sees a styled full-screen backdrop with a centered framed dialog at intro and during play. Why: usability and polish.
acceptance_criteria: Given the app loads, when the intro shows, then it fills the viewport with a background image and the text sits in a centered framed dialog using the pixel fonts.
Given the game is playing, when the screen renders, then the scene fills the whole viewport and the story text appears in a centered dialog rather than a right-hand sidebar.
Given any screen, when text renders, then body text uses VT323 at 16px or larger and headings use Press Start 2P on a dark background with light text.

in_scope: GameLayout full-screen scene and centered story dialog
out_of_scope: Phaser scene logic and game content
preserve: Existing game state, dialogue choices and inventory behavior
Frame kit classes sf-frame-* and sf-btn

technical_constraints: UI-only change in game/frontend; no API changes
Use the existing tokens (--sf-color-*, --sf-font-*, --sf-size-*) and frame kit; do not add remote font URLs
definition_of_done: All requirement slices are implemented and their unit tests pass
non_functional: Text contrast stays readable (light parchment text on dark ink)
